Only a trusted few belonged to the general's inner circle, and every secret whispered there could tip the fate of the entire campaign. （读后续写·权力核心）
Torn between loyalty and honesty, he wrestled with an inner conflict that no one around the dinner table could possibly guess. （读后续写·心理挣扎）

synonyms.example: The company launched an internal investigation to trace the source of the leak. （应用文·正式调查）
synonyms.usage: 辨析:internal 偏客观、正式，指"事物结构或组织内部的"（如 internal organs 内脏、internal affairs 内部事务）；inner 更常指"内心、精神层面"或"物理上更靠里的"，感情色彩更浓。

synonyms.example: In the diary she confided her innermost fears, words she could never have spoken aloud. （读后续写·倾诉秘密）
synonyms.usage: 辨析:innermost 是 inner 的最高级形式，强调"最深、最隐秘的"，语气更强、更文学化；inner 是常态用法，程度较缓。

synonyms.example: She turned her gaze inward, searching her own heart for an answer the world could not give. （读后续写·内省）
synonyms.usage: 辨析:inward 兼作形容词与副词，强调"朝内的方向或内省的过程"；inner 只作形容词，强调"处于内部或属于内心的状态"。

advancedExpressions.expression: inner beauty 内在美 ｜ inner peace 内心平静 ｜ inner strength 内在力量 ｜ inner voice 内心之声 ｜ inner world 内心世界 ｜ inner circle 核心圈 ｜ the inner city 内城区 ｜ inner conflict 内心冲突
advancedExpressions.example: Only when she quieted her inner conflict did she hear her inner voice and find true inner peace. 唯有平息内心冲突，她才听见内心之声，寻得真正的内心平静。（一句串记）

advancedExpressions.expression: inner adj. 内部的/内心的（反义 outer 外部的）→ innermost adj. 最深处的（最高级形式，最隐秘的）｜ 近义 internal（客观正式，如 internal organs 内脏）、inward（可作副/形，朝内的）
advancedExpressions.example: outer space 外太空 vs. inner world 内心世界；in her innermost heart 在她内心最深处（innermost 表'最深'）。

advancedExpressions.expression: inner 内心/物理更靠里，感情色彩浓（inner peace）｜ internal 客观正式'内部的'（internal affairs 内部事务，internal organs 内脏）｜ inward 朝内的方向/内省（既可形容词也可副词：turn inward）
advancedExpressions.example: an internal report（内部报告）／ inner peace（内心平静）／ She turned her gaze inward.（她转向内省）三词各有归属。

advancedExpressions.expression: somewhere deep in her inner world, ... began to ...
advancedExpressions.example: Somewhere deep in her inner world, a long-buried courage began to stir, faint at first, then rising like the tide until it swept every trace of doubt away. （somewhere deep in her inner world 地点状语渲染 + 比喻(rising like the tide) + 渐强节奏，续写结尾升华）

advancedExpressions.expression: let us cultivate our inner ... rather than chase mere ...
advancedExpressions.example: Let us cultivate our inner richness through reading and reflection, rather than chase the fleeting glitter of material things. （let us + rather than 对比呼吁句式，倡议书主体）

advancedExpressions.expression: outward success means little without inner ...
advancedExpressions.example: Outward success means little without inner fulfilment, for a life crowned with achievement yet hollow at its core is a mansion with no one living inside. （outward...without inner 表里对照 + 隐喻(mansion with no one inside)，深化论点）

sentenceUpgrade.original: She felt calm inside.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: As the last echo of applause died away and the lights dimmed, a deep inner calm settled over her — the quiet certainty of one who had finally made peace with who she was. （读后续写·内心平静·舞台落幕）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: As 时间状语从句营造场景 + 环境描写(applause died / lights dimmed) + inner calm settled over her 拟物化 + 破折号补充 + 定语从句点明缘由

sentenceUpgrade.original: We should value our inner qualities, not just our looks.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Rather than obsessing over the fleeting perfection of appearance, we would do well to nurture our inner qualities — kindness, resilience and wisdom — for these alone endure long after youth has faded. （议论文·内在品质）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Rather than 对比开篇 + we would do well to 委婉建议 + 破折号列举(kindness, resilience, wisdom) + for 引导原因 + 时间对照(endure...after youth faded)

classPractice.question: 用 inner 填空：True confidence springs not from outward praise but from an ____ conviction of one's own worth.
classPractice.note: inner conviction 内在信念；与 outward 形成'内/外'对照，本词反义即 outer/outward

classPractice.question: 在 inner / internal 中选：The company launched an ____ investigation to find the source of the leak.
classPractice.note: internal 用于客观、正式的'组织/机构内部'；inner 多指'内心/物理更靠里'

classPractice.question: 你也许需要放下逻辑思维，才能发现一首诗真正的内在美。You might need to abandon logical thinking to discover a poem's true ____ ____.
classPractice.note: inner beauty 内在美——呼应本单元课文；inner 修饰名词表'内在的'

translation: 注意到，意识到；将……理解为，将……视为
original_sentence: As long as the journey of poetry reading makes you feel something or lets you perceive another level of meaning, it will have been worth your effort.
readingExamples: As long as the journey of poetry reading makes you feel something or lets you perceive another level of meaning, it will have been worth your effort.
definitionEn:
(1) vt. to become aware of something through one of the senses, especially sight; to notice or realise
(2) vt. to understand or think of someone or something in a particular way; to regard as
(3) vt. to come to recognise or grasp the true nature of something after careful attention

posExamples.sentence: Only when she read the letter for a third time did she perceive the trembling sorrow hidden beneath its cheerful words, and her eyes filled with sudden tears. （读后续写·细读家书·察觉隐情）
I hope that through this exchange programme, our foreign friends will come to perceive China not as a distant name on a map, but as a warm land of real, kind-hearted people. （应用文·交流活动）
How we perceive failure often matters more than the failure itself, for the same setback that crushes one person may awaken in another an unbreakable resolve. （议论文·看待失败）
Through the thinning mist he gradually perceived the outline of a lighthouse, and with it came a flood of hope he had not felt for days. （读后续写·海上历险·希望重现）

collocations.phrase: perceive colour / a note of unhappiness
collocations.translation: 【课件】察觉/注意到颜色、（声音里）一丝不快（perceive vt. 注意到，意识到，察觉到）
collocations.example: Cats are not able to perceive colour. 猫无法辨别颜色。｜ I perceived a note of unhappiness in her voice. 我察觉到她声音里透着一丝不快。
This discovery was perceived as a major breakthrough. 这一发现被视为一项重大突破。

collocations.phrase: be perceived to be / to do
collocations.translation: 【课件】被认为是……／被认为做……（被动句型）
collocations.example: The national football team is widely perceived to be unlucky. 人们普遍认为国足运气不佳。
Many students perceive mistakes as failures rather than lessons. 许多学生把错误看作失败，而非教训。
Kindness is sometimes wrongly perceived as weakness. 善良有时被误认为软弱。
Returning after ten years, he perceived a change in almost everything. 十年后归来，他察觉几乎一切都变了。
The moment she perceived the danger, she slipped towards the door. 她一察觉到危险，就悄悄溜向门口。
As long as poetry lets you perceive another level of meaning, the effort will never be wasted. 只要诗歌能让你领悟到另一层含义，付出就绝不会白费。（呼应课文）
Distance, she realised, had allowed her to perceive her father's love more clearly than proximity ever had. （读后续写·亲情反思）
The reform, widely perceived as risky at first, gradually won the trust of even its harshest critics. （议论文·社会变革）

collocations.phrase: perceive the world (in a new way)
collocations.example: A single line of poetry can suddenly make us perceive the world in an entirely new way, as if a curtain had been drawn back before our eyes. （议论文·文学的力量）

synonyms.example: She noticed a faint scratch on the old table and wondered what story it might tell. （读后续写·观察细节）
synonyms.usage: 辨析:notice 是最普通的"注意到"，多指对显而易见之物的留意；perceive 更正式、更深，含"通过感官或思考而察觉、领悟"之意，常涉及不易觉察的事物或抽象含义。

synonyms.example: A skilled doctor can detect the earliest signs of illness long before the patient feels unwell. （议论文·专业敏锐）
synonyms.usage: 辨析:detect 侧重"发现隐藏的、不易察觉的事物"（如疾病、谎言、气味），常需专门能力或仪器；perceive 侧重"意识到、理解为"，可指感官也可指认知层面。

synonyms.example: The whole village regarded the old teacher as a father, turning to him in every joy and sorrow. （读后续写·人物地位）
synonyms.usage: 辨析:regard...as 与 perceive...as 都表"视为"，但 regard 更强调主观评价与态度；perceive 强调经由观察或思考"形成的认知"，语气更客观、更书面。

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·perceive + 宾语 + 宾语补足语（课件）
advancedExpressions.expression: perceive sb/sth do 察觉……（强调结果，动作已完成）｜ perceive sb/sth doing 察觉……正在发生 ｜ perceive sb/sth to be / as sth 将……视为；被动句型 sb/sth be perceived to do 被认为做……
advancedExpressions.example: Nobody perceived him enter/entering the warehouse. 没人察觉他进（正进）仓库。｜ The patient was perceived to have difficulty in breathing. 有人发现病人呼吸困难。（被动 sb be perceived to do）

advancedExpressions.expression: perceive sth 察觉/意识到 ｜ perceive sth as sth 把……视为 ｜ be perceived as 被视为 ｜ perceive that + 从句 意识到…… ｜ perceive sb do/doing 察觉某人做（感官动词接省to不定式或-ing）
advancedExpressions.example: She perceived him watching her（察觉他在看她）and perceived that something was wrong（意识到不对劲）, though most would perceive the room as calm（视房间为平静）. 三种结构一句呈现。

advancedExpressions.expression: perceive v. → perception n. 感知/看法（重点名词）→ perceptive adj. 有洞察力的（人）→ perceptible adj. 可察觉的（事物）→ perceptively adv. ｜ 同源 receive→reception, deceive→deception（ceive→ception 变形）
advancedExpressions.example: Her sharp perception（洞察）let her perceive（察觉）what a less perceptive（敏锐）person would have missed. perceive→perception→perceptive 一句串。

advancedExpressions.expression: notice 最普通'注意到'（显而易见之物）｜ perceive 更正式深，'经感官/思考而察觉、领悟'（含抽象、不易察觉之物）｜ regard...as 强调主观评价态度，perceive...as 强调经观察'形成的认知'
advancedExpressions.example: She noticed the scratch（注意到划痕，表面）but perceived its hidden meaning（领悟其深意，深层）. notice 浅、perceive 深。

advancedExpressions.expression: only then did she perceive that ...
advancedExpressions.example: Only then did she perceive that the silence between them had never been coldness, but a love too deep for words. （only then did 倒装 + perceive that 引导宾语从句 + not...but 揭示真相，续写顿悟段）

advancedExpressions.expression: we invite you to perceive ... from a fresh perspective
advancedExpressions.example: We warmly invite every visitor to perceive our ancient craft from a fresh perspective, and to feel the heartbeat of tradition in each handmade piece. （invite sb to perceive...from a fresh perspective 邀请句式，宣传文体）

advancedExpressions.expression: the way we perceive ... shapes the way we ...
advancedExpressions.example: The way we perceive the world quietly shapes the way we live in it; change the lens, and the very same reality glows with new colour. （the way we perceive...shapes the way we... 因果句式 + 隐喻(change the lens)，点明论点）

sentenceUpgrade.original: She saw that he was sad.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Though he forced a bright smile and spoke of cheerful things, she perceived at once the shadow of grief flickering behind his eyes, and her heart ached with a sympathy she dared not voice. （读后续写·察言观色·细腻心理）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Though 让步状语从句 + perceived at once 替换 saw 提升层次 + 隐喻(shadow of grief flickering) + 递进心理描写(heart ached...dared not voice)

sentenceUpgrade.original: People see problems differently.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: How individuals perceive the very same problem varies enormously, for each of us views the world through a lens ground by our own experiences, hopes and fears. （议论文·主观认知）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: How 引导主语从句 + perceive 精准动词 + for 引导原因分句 + 隐喻(lens ground by experiences) + 三名词并列(experiences, hopes, fears)增强气势

classPractice.question: 【课件】When in senior high school, he ____ (perceive) the relationship between success and effort.
classPractice.note: 叙述过去发生的领悟，用一般过去时 perceived；perceive 意识到/察觉到

classPractice.question: 【课件】Most blind people, even if they don't have any sight, are still able ____ (perceive) light.
classPractice.note: be able to do sth 有能力做某事，故用不定式 to perceive

classPractice.question: Kindness is often wrongly ____ ____ weakness, yet it takes real strength to be gentle. （被视为）
classPractice.note: be perceived as 被视为/被认为是；perceive sth as sth 的被动形式——本单元重点

classPractice.question: Her sharp ____ (perceive) allowed her to sense what others had missed.
classPractice.note: perceive v. → perception n. 感知/洞察力；此处作句子主语需名词

classPractice.question: 在 notice / perceive 中选最正式贴切：Reading between the lines, she ____ a hidden sorrow beneath his cheerful words.
classPractice.note: perceive 强调'经思考领悟不易察觉之物'；notice 仅指'注意到显而易见之物'

translation: 现实，实际情况；事实，实际存在
original_sentence: Poetry’s combination of “sound” and “sense” makes you see the world in a new way and allows you to go beyond normal reality for the everlasting beauty.
readingExamples: Poetry’s combination of “sound” and “sense” makes you see the world in a new way and allows you to go beyond normal reality for the everlasting beauty.
definitionEn:
(1) n. the true situation and the things that actually exist, rather than an imagined or desired one
(2) n. something that actually exists or happens; a fact
(3) n. the quality of being lifelike or true to actual experience
(4) n. the state of things as they are, especially as opposed to a hoped-for or ideal version

posExamples.sentence: For one dizzying moment she thought she was still dreaming, but the cold rain on her face dragged her sharply back to reality — the ship was truly gone. （读后续写·梦醒·残酷现实）
I am writing to remind fellow students that behind the glamorous images online lies a far harsher reality, and we should never measure our own lives against a screen. （应用文·倡议信）
Great poetry allows us to go beyond ordinary reality, and yet, paradoxically, it returns us to daily life with eyes that see its hidden wonders anew. （议论文·文学与现实·呼应课文）
The harsh reality of the drought could no longer be denied, and the once-proud farmer stood in his cracked field, watching his life's work wither before his eyes. （读后续写·灾难·直面现实）

idioms.translation: 事实上，实际上（常用来对比表象）
idioms.example: He appeared calm and confident on stage, but in reality his knees were trembling and his mouth had gone dry. （读后续写·表里反差·舞台紧张）

idioms.translation: ……的残酷现实
idioms.example: No fairy tale had prepared her for the harsh reality of standing alone in a strange city with an empty purse and a heavy heart. （读后续写·独闯异乡）

collocations.translation: 事实上，实际上（常对比表象）
collocations.example: He seemed calm, but in reality he was terrified. 他看似镇定，实际上却怕得要命。
Sooner or later we must all face reality. 我们迟早都得面对现实。
After years of effort, her dream finally became a reality. 多年努力后，她的梦想终于成真。
Through virtual reality, students walked among ancient ruins without leaving the classroom. 借助虚拟现实，学生不出教室就漫步于古迹之中。
Losing himself in video games was, he admitted, merely a way to escape the reality he was too afraid to change. （议论文·逃避与担当）
The reality is that talent without discipline rarely blossoms, and discipline can carry an ordinary person further than talent alone. （议论文·天赋与努力）
The shrill ring of the alarm brought her back to reality, and the golden palace of her dream crumbled into the grey of an ordinary morning. （读后续写·梦醒时分）
Young children cannot always distinguish fantasy from reality, which is why the stories we tell them matter so deeply. （议论文·童年教育）

collocations.phrase: the harsh / grim / cruel reality of ...
collocations.example: No fairy tale had prepared her for the harsh reality of standing alone in a strange city with an empty purse. （读后续写·独闯异乡）

synonyms.example: Whatever excuses he offered, the fact remained that he had broken his solemn promise. （议论文·事实为据）
synonyms.usage: 辨析:fact 指"单个确凿的事实"，可数、具体；reality 指"整体的现实状况"，多不可数，强调与幻想／理想相对的"真实境况"。

synonyms.example: The truth, painful as it was, finally set her free from years of self-deception. （读后续写·真相与解脱）
synonyms.usage: 辨析:truth 强调"与谎言、错误相对的真相或真理"，含价值判断；reality 强调"客观存在的实际情况"，与"想象、理想"相对，不必涉及是非。

synonyms.example: What looked simple in theory proved, in actuality, to be riddled with unforeseen difficulties. （议论文·理论与实践）
synonyms.usage: 辨析:actuality 较正式书面，强调"实际发生／存在的状态"，常用于 in actuality 对比理论与现实；reality 更常用、更口语通用。

advancedExpressions.expression: in reality 实际上 ｜ face/confront reality 面对现实 ｜ become a reality 成为现实 ｜ escape (from) reality 逃避现实 ｜ bring sb back to reality 把某人拉回现实 ｜ virtual reality 虚拟现实 ｜ the harsh reality of 残酷现实
advancedExpressions.example: He preferred to escape reality, but a phone call brought him back to reality and forced him to face the harsh reality of the situation. 他宁愿逃避现实，但一通电话把他拉回现实，逼他直面严峻的现实。（一句串记）

advancedExpressions.expression: reality n. 现实 → real adj. 真实的 → really adv. 真正地 → realise/realize v. 意识到/实现 → realistic adj. 现实的/逼真的 → realism n. 现实主义 → unreal/unrealistic adj. 不真实/不切实际的
advancedExpressions.example: It was hard to realise that this real, everyday reality was once only an unrealistic dream. 很难意识到这真实的日常现实曾只是不切实际的梦想。（real/reality/realise/unrealistic 同族一句）

advancedExpressions.expression: reality（整体'现实状况'，多不可数，与幻想/理想相对）｜ fact（单个确凿'事实'，可数具体）｜ truth（'真相/真理'，与谎言错误相对，含价值判断）
advancedExpressions.example: The fact（一个事实）is undeniable; the truth（真相）is painful; but such is the reality（现实境况）we must accept. 三词一句见区别。

advancedExpressions.expression: reality came crashing down / rushing back
advancedExpressions.example: For a heartbeat the world was perfect — and then reality came crashing down, cold and merciless, as the referee's whistle announced their defeat. （reality came crashing down 拟人化冲击 + 破折号制造转折 + 环境呼应，续写高潮转折）

advancedExpressions.expression: we must not lose sight of the reality that ...
advancedExpressions.example: In our pursuit of a greener campus, we must not lose sight of the reality that lasting change begins with the small habits of each individual. （we must not lose sight of the reality that 提醒句式，倡议信深化）

advancedExpressions.expression: the gap between the ideal and reality is bridged not by ... but by ...
advancedExpressions.example: The gap between the ideal and reality is bridged not by wishful dreaming, but by patient, day-to-day action. （the gap between ideal and reality 对照 + not...but 强调途径，升华论点）

sentenceUpgrade.original: Her dream came true at last.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The dream she had nursed through countless discouraging nights at last became a shining reality, and standing on that stage beneath a thousand lights, she could scarcely believe the trembling girl of years ago had come so far. （读后续写·梦想成真·今昔对照）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 定语从句(she had nursed through...nights) + became a shining reality 升级搭配 + 环境描写(beneath a thousand lights) + 今昔对照(the trembling girl of years ago)增强感染力

sentenceUpgrade.original: Life is not as easy as we imagine.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The reality of life is often far more unforgiving than our youthful imagination paints it, yet it is precisely in wrestling with that hard truth that we forge the strength to endure. （议论文·理想与现实）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: the reality of life 名词化主语 + far more...than 比较级强化 + 隐喻(imagination paints) + yet 转折 + it is precisely...that 强调句 + forge the strength 生动动词

classPractice.question: He appeared confident on stage, but ____ ____ his knees were trembling. （实际上）
classPractice.note: in reality 实际上，常用于对比表象与真相——本单元重点短语

classPractice.question: After ten years of effort, the dream of a village library finally became ____ ____ (real).
classPractice.note: become a reality 成为现实；real adj. → reality n.，此处需名词并加不定冠词

classPractice.question: 在 reality / truth 中选：The ____, painful as it was, finally set her free from years of self-deception.
classPractice.note: truth 指'与谎言相对的真相'含价值判断；reality 指'客观现实境况'与幻想相对

translation: 薄雾，水汽
original_sentence: The universal language 21 B Applying the rules B1 Circle the mistakes and write down the correct forms in the blanks.
readingExamples: The universal language 21 B Applying the rules B1 Circle the mistakes and write down the correct forms in the blanks.
definitionEn:
(1) n. a cloud of very small drops of water in the air just above the ground, that makes it difficult to see
(2) n. a thin film or blur on a surface, such as steam or condensation on glass
(3) v. to become covered with tiny drops of water, so that it is hard to see through; to fill with tears
(4) n. (literary) something that prevents you from thinking clearly or seeing the truth

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (眼睛)因泪水而模糊;使朦胧
uncommonMeanings.example: As the old sailor spoke of the shipmates he had lost, his eyes misted over, and for a long moment he could not go on. （读后续写·情感·哽咽）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (遮蔽认知的)迷雾,朦胧感
uncommonMeanings.example: For years grief had hung over him like a mist, blurring every joy; only now, watching his grandson laugh, did the fog begin to lift. （读后续写·心理·走出悲伤）

posExamples.sentence: A thin mist crept across the valley at dawn, and the mountains seemed to float, half-dissolved, like a landscape from a forgotten dream — Lucy caught her breath at the sheer beauty of it. （读后续写·景物描写·清晨徒步）
I am writing to remind all members that the early-morning mist on our campus lake can seriously reduce visibility, so cyclists are kindly advised to slow down and switch on their lights. （应用文·通知）
Just as a mist obscures the road ahead yet cannot alter its true direction, temporary confusion may cloud our judgement, but it should never make us abandon the goals we have set. （议论文·坚持目标）
The bathroom mirror had misted up completely, so she wrote her little brother's name in the fog with a fingertip before wiping it clear. （读后续写·生活细节·亲情）

wordForms.other: mistiness (n. 多雾;朦胧)

idioms.translation: 遥远而模糊的过去,时间的迷雾
idioms.example: The true origin of the festival is lost in the mists of time, yet every autumn the whole village still gathers to light the lanterns. （读后续写·传统习俗）

idioms.idiom: lost in a mist / in a mist
idioms.translation: 茫然,不知所措
idioms.example: For the first weeks in the new school she moved as if in a mist, unable to tell one corridor from another. （读后续写·转学·迷茫）

collocations.example: The hills faded away in the mist. 群山在雾中渐渐隐去。

collocations.phrase: a mist of tears (课堂·熟词僻义)
collocations.example: She saw his face through a mist of tears. 她透过泪雾看着他的脸。
By noon the mist had lifted. 到中午雾就散了。
A thick mist rolled in from the sea, swallowing the lighthouse until only its faint, blinking light remained. （读后续写·海边·氛围渲染）
A light mist still clung to the meadow when the campers unzipped their tents to greet the first grey light. （读后续写·露营）
The ancient temple, shrouded in mist, appeared and vanished like a memory that refused to be pinned down. （读后续写·古迹·神秘感）
By mid-morning the mist had lifted, revealing a golden patchwork of ripening fields that stretched to the horizon. （读后续写·景物转折）
With a final wave, the ferry slipped away and vanished into the mist, leaving the boy alone on the trembling pier. （读后续写·离别）
As the temperature dropped, a silvery mist rose from the river and drifted between the sleeping houses. （读后续写·夜晚小镇）
Through the mist she could just make out a figure waving frantically, and her heart leapt — he had come after all. （读后续写·重逢）

synonyms.example: The fog was so dense that the driver could barely see the bonnet of his own car, let alone the road ahead. （读后续写·恶劣天气）
synonyms.usage: 辨析核心：浓度不同。fog 最浓、能见度最低、危险，常致交通事故，可作气象警报词；mist 轻薄朦胧、常带诗意美感，续写写氛围首选 mist。二者皆不可数。

synonyms.example: A summer haze shimmered above the distant hills, softening their edges into a dreamy blur. （读后续写·夏日景色）
synonyms.usage: haze 多由高温、尘埃或轻烟造成，能见度受影响但不像水汽那样湿润；mist 专指近地面的细小水珠，湿润、成片可见。

synonyms.example: White vapour curled from the mug of hot cocoa, warming her frozen fingers as she cupped it close. （读后续写·冬日温暖）
synonyms.usage: vapour 泛指气态水汽或蒸汽，偏科学/中性；mist 特指飘浮在空气中、可见成片的水珠，画面感更强。

advancedExpressions.expression: As the mist began to lift, so too did ...
advancedExpressions.example: As the mist began to lift, so too did the heaviness in her heart, and for the first time in months she smiled at the brightening sky. （景物与心情同步的"环境映心"技法）

advancedExpressions.expression: In view of the frequent morning mist, we advise ...
advancedExpressions.example: In view of the frequent morning mist along the mountain trail, we strongly advise participants to stay together and keep a whistle within reach. （通知类文体·委婉提醒句式）

advancedExpressions.expression: just as mist ... , so ...
advancedExpressions.example: Just as a passing mist can never dim the sun for long, momentary failures cannot extinguish the ambition of one who is truly determined.

sentenceUpgrade.original: There was mist everywhere and I felt sad.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: A cold mist wound itself around the empty streets like a slow grey breath, and something in its silence seemed to press against my chest, until the sadness I had been holding back finally spilled over. （读后续写·情景交融）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 拟人(wound itself like a breath) + 明喻(like a slow grey breath) + 环境映心(mist的压抑感投射内心) + 情感层层推进

sentenceUpgrade.original: In the morning there was mist over the fields.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: At first light, a delicate mist lay draped across the fields, muffling every sound, so that the whole world seemed to be holding its breath, waiting for the day to begin. （读后续写·清晨氛围）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 过去分词短语作状语(draped) + 拟人(holding its breath) + 现在分词后置(muffling, waiting)营造静谧感

classPractice.question: As the sun rose, the ____ (mist) valley slowly emerged from the grey haze.
classPractice.note: 考 mist 的形容词形式 misty（多雾的），修饰名词 valley。

classPractice.question: 选 mist / fog 填空：The ____ was so thick that all flights were cancelled and drivers crawled along at walking pace.
classPractice.note: 辨析：能见度极低、造成危险/停航时用 fog（浓雾）；薄而带美感的用 mist。

classPractice.question: 透过泪雾，她几乎看不清母亲的脸。Through a ____ ____ ____, she could hardly make out her mother's face.
classPractice.note: 考熟词僻义搭配 a mist of tears（泪雾），mist 在此比喻模糊的视线。

translation: 小说家
original_sentence: It was a time when many painters, musicians, novelists and poets looked at the world in new and different ways.
readingExamples: It was a time when many painters, musicians, novelists and poets looked at the world in new and different ways.
definitionEn:
(1) n. a person who writes novels; a writer of long works of prose fiction
(2) n. (broadly) a professional author known for creating imaginative stories and characters

posExamples.sentence: The shy, ink-stained girl who once hid her stories in a shoebox had, against every expectation, grown into a novelist whose books now filled the very shelves she used to gaze at longingly. （读后续写·梦想成真·人物成长）
I am writing to invite you to our literary festival, where a celebrated novelist will share how ordinary life can be transformed into unforgettable fiction. （应用文·邀请信）
A great novelist does more than entertain; through vivid characters and moral dilemmas, he holds up a mirror to society and quietly urges us to become better human beings. （议论文·文学的价值）
As a budding novelist myself, I know how daunting the blank page can feel, which is why I would love to join the school's creative-writing club and grow alongside fellow story-lovers. （应用文·申请信）

wordForms.noun: novelist (小说家); novel (小说); novella (中篇小说)
wordForms.adjective: novelistic (小说的,小说家的); novel (adj. 新颖的——同形异义,拼写相同)
wordForms.other: 构词法·-ist 表'从事…的人/…主义者'：novel→novelist(小说家)，同类 artist(艺术家)、scientist(科学家)、pianist(钢琴家)、journalist(记者)。词族：novel(小说) / novelist(小说家) / novelistic(小说的)。易混：novel 作名词=小说，作形容词=新颖的，同形不同义，需按语境判断。

collocations.example: The novel was written by a famous novelist. 这部小说出自一位著名小说家之手。
She dreamed of becoming a novelist. 她梦想成为一名小说家。
The lecture hall was packed, for a renowned novelist had agreed to reveal the secrets behind her best-selling series. （应用文·活动报道）

collocations.translation: 有抱负的 / 崭露头角的小说家
collocations.example: An aspiring novelist at heart, he filled notebook after notebook long before anyone believed his stories were worth reading. （读后续写·坚持梦想）
So prolific a novelist was she that a new title appeared on the shelves almost every spring, each more daring than the last. （读后续写·倒装·人物介绍）
Few of his classmates guessed that the quiet boy scribbling in the back row would one day become a novelist read across the world. （读后续写·蜕变）
The essay compares a nineteenth-century master with a contemporary novelist to show how storytelling has evolved. （议论文·文学比较）
Immersing herself in the works of the novelist, she began to understand how a single detail could carry the weight of an entire life. （读后续写·阅读感悟）

synonyms.example: The young author signed copies for a queue that stretched right out of the bookshop door. （应用文·签售报道）
synonyms.usage: author 泛指任何书籍/文章的作者（含非虚构、教材等）;novelist 专指写长篇小说的人,范围更窄

synonyms.example: She had always thought of herself as a writer, though it took years before she dared call herself a novelist. （读后续写·身份认同）
synonyms.usage: writer 最宽泛,记者、编剧、诗人皆可称之;novelist 特指小说创作者,更正式、更具体

synonyms.example: Even without a single published book, her grandfather was the finest storyteller she had ever known. （读后续写·亲情·口述故事）
synonyms.usage: storyteller 强调"会讲故事"这一才能,可以是口头的、非书面的;novelist 一定是写成书的职业创作者

advancedExpressions.expression: the ... who once ... had become a novelist ...
advancedExpressions.example: The timid child who once feared to read aloud in class had become a novelist whose words now gave courage to thousands of readers just like her former self. （今昔对照+首尾呼应,升华梦想主题）

advancedExpressions.expression: we are honoured to have ... , a novelist renowned for ...
advancedExpressions.example: We are honoured to have Mr. Lin, a novelist renowned for his vivid portraits of rural China, deliver the keynote speech at this year's Reading Week. （邀请信·正式介绍嘉宾）

advancedExpressions.expression: a true novelist not only ... but also ...
advancedExpressions.example: A true novelist not only weaves an engaging plot but also illuminates the hidden corners of the human heart, teaching us empathy long after the last page is turned.

sentenceUpgrade.original: She wanted to be a novelist and worked hard.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Determined to become a novelist, she rose before dawn each day to fill another page, trusting that every rejected manuscript was merely a stepping stone toward the story only she could tell. （读后续写·励志）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 过去分词短语作状语(Determined to...) + 现在分词伴随(trusting that...) + 比喻(stepping stone) + 细节动作(rose before dawn)

sentenceUpgrade.original: The novelist wrote about real life, so people liked his books.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Because the novelist drew his characters straight from the streets he knew so well, readers everywhere saw their own joys and struggles reflected in his pages, and his books were embraced with rare affection. （议论文·文学感染力）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 原因状语从句前置 + 隐喻(drew from the streets) + 结果句升级(were embraced with rare affection替代liked) + 高级搭配

classPractice.question: Mo Yan, a famous ____ (novel), won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2012.
classPractice.note: 考构词法 -ist：novel + ist → novelist（小说家）；指人用 novelist，不用 novel。

classPractice.question: 选 novel / novelist：Her latest ____ tells the story of three generations of one family.
classPractice.note: 作品（小说）用 novel；写小说的人（小说家）用 novelist。此处主语是'作品'。

classPractice.question: 许多画家、音乐家、小说家和诗人开始用新的方式看世界。Many painters, musicians, ____ and poets began to look at the world in new ways.
classPractice.note: 呼应课文原句；与其他并列名词一致，用复数 novelists。

translation: 与某事物断绝关系，摒弃
original_sentence: Breakfast is an important meal and what people eat for breakfast is quite different.
readingExamples: Breakfast is an important meal and what people eat for breakfast is quite different.
definitionEn:
(1) v. to end a relationship, connection, or association with something, especially a tradition, belief, or past way of doing things
(2) v. to deliberately stop following an established custom, convention, or group
(3) v. to make a clear, decisive departure from something that came before

posExamples.sentence: For the first time in her life she decided to break with the timid habits of the past, squared her shoulders, and walked straight up to the microphone. （读后续写·突破自我）
I strongly suggest that our class break with the outdated practice of copying model essays and instead encourage students to write freely from their own experience. （应用文·建议信）
To make real progress, a society must occasionally break with tradition, for customs that once served us well can, in time, become the very chains that hold us back. （议论文·革新与传统）
The young director boldly broke with convention, filming the entire scene in a single unbroken shot that left the audience breathless. （读后续写·艺术创新）

idioms.translation: 打破传统 / 与过去决裂
idioms.example: They decided to break with tradition and hold the wedding outdoors. 他们决定打破传统，在户外举办婚礼。

idioms.translation: 与……彻底决裂，一刀两断
idioms.example: After years of quarrels, she made a clean break with her old life. 争吵多年后，她与旧生活彻底一刀两断。

collocations.example: By inviting parents to grade the projects, the teacher broke with convention and gave the whole class a fresh sense of purpose. （读后续写·教育创新）
Moving to a new city gave him the courage to break with the past and finally build the life he had always imagined. （读后续写·重新开始）

collocations.phrase: break with the old ways / customs
collocations.translation: 摒弃旧方式 / 旧习俗
collocations.example: The village elders were reluctant to break with the old ways, yet the younger generation quietly pushed for change. （议论文·代际观念冲突）

collocations.translation: 打破常规,改变一成不变的生活
collocations.example: Determined to break with routine, the family packed a tent and drove off toward mountains none of them had ever seen. （读后续写·家庭·冒险）
The Romantic poets deliberately broke with the established rules of composition, prizing feeling and imagination above rigid form. （议论文·文学史·呼应课文）

collocations.phrase: make a clean break with sth
collocations.example: It took enormous willpower, but she finally made a clean break with the habits that had held her back for years. （读后续写·戒除·成长）

synonyms.example: He abandoned the safe career his parents had chosen for him and set out to become a painter. （读后续写·追梦）
synonyms.usage: abandon 强调彻底放弃某物/某人,可用于具体或抽象;break with 特指切断与传统、习惯、群体的"联系",带"决裂"意味

synonyms.example: The new curriculum departs from the exam-centred model in favour of hands-on learning. （议论文·教育改革）
synonyms.usage: depart from 较中性、书面,指偏离某标准/常规;break with 情感更强烈,含"主动、决然地断绝"的意味

synonyms.example: In her speech she publicly renounced the prejudices she had once quietly accepted. （议论文·正式文体）
synonyms.usage: renounce 非常正式,强调公开、正式地放弃权利/信仰/立场;break with 更口语、日常,搭配 tradition/past 等最自然

advancedExpressions.type: 短语群·'与…决裂/打破'一组
advancedExpressions.expression: break with sth / depart from sth / do away with sth / make a clean break with sth
advancedExpressions.example: To move forward, the reformers had to break with tradition, depart from old routines and do away with rules that no longer served anyone. 要前进，改革者必须与传统决裂、背离旧例、废除不再有用的规矩。（同义短语群，写作可替换升级）

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·break 的不规则变化
advancedExpressions.expression: break - broke - broken；短语 break with 的过去式作 broke with
advancedExpressions.example: The moment she broke with the fear that had ruled her, everything changed. 她与恐惧决裂的那一刻，一切都变了。（注意过去式 broke，过去分词 broken）

advancedExpressions.expression: the moment sb. broke with ... , everything changed
advancedExpressions.example: The moment she broke with the fear that had ruled her for so long, everything changed — her voice steadied, her eyes lifted, and the room fell silent in respect. （以"决裂时刻"为转折点，动作三连描写）

advancedExpressions.expression: it is high time we broke with ... and embraced ...
advancedExpressions.example: It is high time we broke with the wasteful habit of single-use plastics and embraced a greener campus for everyone. （倡议书·it is high time + 虚拟语气过去式）

advancedExpressions.expression: to break with ... does not mean to abandon ... entirely
advancedExpressions.example: To break with outdated customs does not mean to abandon our heritage entirely; rather, it means having the wisdom to keep what nourishes us and let go of what no longer does.

sentenceUpgrade.original: She stopped following old habits and became braver.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The day she resolved to break with the timid habits of a lifetime, a quiet courage took root in her chest, and she found herself doing the very things that had once seemed unthinkable. （读后续写·蜕变）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 时间状语前置(The day...) + 隐喻(courage took root) + 结果句(found herself doing...) + break with短语替代平淡表达

sentenceUpgrade.original: We should not always follow tradition.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: While tradition deserves our respect, we must be brave enough to break with it whenever it stands in the way of progress, for blind obedience to the past is the surest way to stall the future. （议论文·辩证）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: While让步状语从句 + break with精准短语 + for引导原因论证 + 格言式收尾(the surest way to...)

classPractice.question: The young director boldly ____ ____ convention, filming the whole scene in a single shot. （用 break 的适当形式）
classPractice.note: 考习语 break with sth（打破/背离）；一般过去时，break 的过去式为 broke。

classPractice.question: 浪漫主义者的目标是与18世纪的理想决裂。The aim of the Romantics was to ____ ____ the ideals of the 18th century.
classPractice.note: 呼应课文；不定式后用原形 break with，意为'与…决裂'。

classPractice.question: They decided to make a clean break with their old habits. → They decided to ____ ____ their old habits completely.
classPractice.note: make a clean break with = break with…completely，'与…彻底决裂'。

translation: n. 理想；典范 | adj. 完美的，理想的
original_sentence: The aim of the Romantics was to break with the ideals of the 18th century: they refused to follow rigid rules; instead, they put emphasis on the importance of imagination and feeling, the love of nature and a return to the past.
readingExamples: The aim of the Romantics was to break with the ideals of the 18th century: they refused to follow rigid rules; instead, they put emphasis on the importance of imagination and feeling, the love of nature and a return to the past.
definitionEn:
(1) n. a principle, standard, or value that one aims for or believes to be worth striving toward
(2) n. a person or thing regarded as a perfect example; a model of excellence
(3) adj. the best possible; exactly right or most suitable for a particular purpose
(4) adj. existing only in the imagination; desirable but not likely to become real

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 仅存在于观念中的,理想化而不现实的
uncommonMeanings.example: In an ideal world no child would ever go to bed hungry; yet the letters piling up on the charity's desk told a far harsher story. （议论文·理想与现实对照）

posExamples.sentence: Even after years of hardship had worn him down, the old teacher clung to the ideal that education could lift any child out of darkness — and that quiet faith lit up every lesson he gave. （读后续写·坚守信念·人物）
With its calm reading corners and gentle lighting, the new library is an ideal place for students to lose themselves in a good book after a long day. （应用文·场所介绍）
The Romantics sought to break with the ideals of an earlier age, prizing imagination and feeling over cold, rigid reason — a rebellion that reshaped art forever. （议论文·文学史·呼应课文）
I believe you would be an ideal candidate for the volunteer programme, for your patience and warmth are exactly what the children need. （应用文·推荐信）

wordForms.noun: ideal (理想); idealism (理想主义); idealist (理想主义者); ideality (n. 理想性)
wordForms.adjective: ideal (理想的); idealistic (理想主义的)
wordForms.adverb: ideally (理想地;最好;非常适合地)
wordForms.other: 词族全家桶：ideal(理想的/理想) / ideally(理想地,最好) / idealism(理想主义) / idealist(理想主义者) / idealistic(理想主义的) / idealize(使理想化)。构词法·-ism 表'主义'、-ist 表'…主义者'、-ize 表'使…化'、-ly 构副词。语义提示：ideal 作形容词=最合适/完美的，作名词=追求的信念（复数 ideals 尤指崇高理想）。

collocations.translation: 【课件】理想、准则；典范（a principle, idea, or standard）
collocations.example: He is the ideal of how a soldier should be. 他是军人应有样子的典范。

collocations.phrase: meet / live up to one's ideals
collocations.translation: 【课件】达到/不辜负某人的理想标准
collocations.example: He always tried to live up to his ideals. 他总是努力不辜负自己的理想。
The young painter never abandoned his artistic ideals. 这位年轻画家从未放弃自己的艺术理想。
He is the ideal of how a soldier should be. 他是军人应有样子的典范。

collocations.translation: 【课件】对……是理想的、非常合适的
collocations.example: The beach is ideal for a holiday. 这个海滩是度假的理想去处。

collocations.translation: 理想的解决办法 / 场所
collocations.example: This quiet park is an ideal place to relax. 这个安静的公园是放松的理想场所。
He never gave up his ideals. 他从未放弃自己的理想。
The summer camp offered an ideal opportunity for shy students to make friends and discover hidden talents. （应用文·活动推荐）
Calm under pressure and endlessly patient, she proved to be the ideal person to lead the rescue team through the storm. （读后续写·人物·危机领导）
The conditions were far from ideal — rain lashing the tents, food running low — yet no one uttered a single complaint. （读后续写·逆境）
Every morning he reminded himself to live up to the ideal of kindness his grandmother had passed down. （读后续写·家风传承）

collocations.phrase: cling to / hold on to an ideal
collocations.example: Though the world grew increasingly cynical, the young journalist clung to the ideal that the truth was always worth telling. （议论文·坚守理想）
The founders started the free clinic with high ideals and empty pockets, driven only by a stubborn belief that everyone deserved care. （议论文·公益·理想）

collocations.translation: 理想世界（常用于对比现实）
collocations.example: In an ideal world, hard work alone would guarantee success; in reality, luck and circumstance also play their part. （议论文·辩证）
With her fluent English and boundless energy, she is ideally suited to the role of exchange-programme guide. （应用文·推荐信）

synonyms.example: It was a perfect afternoon — clear skies, a gentle breeze, and not a single worry on their minds. （读后续写·美好场景）
synonyms.usage: perfect 强调"毫无缺陷",绝对化;ideal 强调"最适合某目的"或"心目中的理想",更常搭配 for/place/candidate

synonyms.example: The retired nurse became a model of selfless devotion that inspired the whole community. （议论文·榜样）
synonyms.usage: model 作名词指"值得效仿的典范";ideal 作名词更抽象,可指"追求的信念/标准",不一定是具体某人

synonyms.example: Researchers searched for the optimal temperature at which the seeds would germinate fastest. （议论文·科学论证）
synonyms.usage: optimal 偏学术、正式,强调"经过权衡后的最佳";ideal 更日常通用,书面口语皆宜

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·'理想的/最合适的'(功能:替换 very good)
advancedExpressions.expression: an ideal ... / the perfect ... / a most suitable ... / ideally suited to ...
advancedExpressions.example: This sunlit corner is an ideal spot to read — indeed, ideally suited to anyone who longs for quiet. 这个洒满阳光的角落是理想的读书处——的确非常适合渴望安静的人。（写作用 ideal 替代平淡的 very good）

advancedExpressions.expression: no matter how ... , sb. never let go of the ideal that ...
advancedExpressions.example: No matter how fiercely the storms of doubt raged, she never let go of the ideal that one honest voice could still make a difference. （让步+隐喻(storms of doubt)，升华人物信念）

advancedExpressions.expression: sb. would be an ideal choice for ... , given ...
advancedExpressions.example: Given her creativity and team spirit, Lisa would be an ideal choice for editor of the school magazine. （推荐信·given引出理由）

advancedExpressions.expression: in an ideal world ... ; in reality, however ...
advancedExpressions.example: In an ideal world, talent alone would open every door; in reality, however, it is perseverance that carries us across the threshold of success.

sentenceUpgrade.original: This place is very good for reading.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Bathed in soft afternoon light and hushed as a chapel, the sunlit corner by the window is an ideal spot to sink into a story and forget the passing hours. （应用文·场所描写）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 过去分词短语作状语(Bathed in...) + 明喻(hushed as a chapel) + 生动动词(sink into) + ideal精准替代good

sentenceUpgrade.original: He always believed in his ideals and never gave up.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Through every setback and every sneer, he held fast to his ideals like a sailor gripping the wheel in a storm, refusing to let the world talk him out of the good he knew was possible. （读后续写·坚守）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 介词短语开头强调逆境 + 明喻(like a sailor gripping the wheel) + 现在分词伴随(refusing to...) + hold fast to升级搭配

classPractice.question: With her patience and warmth, Anna is ____ (ideal) suited to working with young children.
classPractice.note: 考副词形式 ideally（非常适合地），修饰形容词 suited，构成 be ideally suited to。

classPractice.question: 选 ideal(n.) / ideal(adj.)：Even in hard times, the old teacher clung to the ____ that education could change lives.
classPractice.note: the ideal that... 用名词 ideal（理想、信念），后接同位语从句；此处考名词用法。

classPractice.question: 在理想世界里，努力就能保证成功。____ ____ ____ ____, hard work alone would guarantee success.
classPractice.note: 固定搭配 in an ideal world（在理想世界里），常与虚拟/对比现实连用；ideal 作形容词。

translation: 死板的，僵硬的；固执的，僵化的
original_sentence: The aim of the Romantics was to break with the ideals of the 18th century: they refused to follow rigid rules; instead, they put emphasis on the importance of imagination and feeling, the love of nature and a return to the past.
readingExamples: The aim of the Romantics was to break with the ideals of the 18th century: they refused to follow rigid rules; instead, they put emphasis on the importance of imagination and feeling, the love of nature and a return to the past.
definitionEn:
(1) adj. (of methods, systems, or rules) very strict, fixed, and difficult to change; unwilling to adapt
(2) adj. (of a person) unwilling to change one's ideas or behaviour; inflexible in attitude
(3) adj. (of an object or material) stiff and hard; not able to be bent or moved
(4) adj. (of the body) stiff and unable to move, often because of fear, cold, or shock

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (因恐惧/寒冷等)僵住的,一动不动的
uncommonMeanings.example: At the sudden crash from the attic, she froze, rigid with terror, every muscle locked as she strained to catch the faintest sound. （读后续写·恐惧·身体反应）

posExamples.sentence: Refusing to bend the rigid rules even once, the old headmaster turned the trembling boy away — a decision he would come to regret for the rest of his days. （读后续写·严苛·悔恨）
I would like to suggest that the club relax its rigid attendance policy, since many members are willing to help but cannot make every single meeting. （应用文·建议信）
The Romantics rebelled against the rigid conventions of their time, arguing that art should flow from genuine feeling rather than obey a set of lifeless rules. （议论文·文学史·呼应课文）
The moment the teacher called her name, Emma sat rigid in her chair, her fingers gripping the desk as if it were the only solid thing left in the room. （读后续写·紧张·身体僵直）

collocations.example: They refused to follow such rigid rules. 他们拒绝遵守这样死板的规则。

collocations.translation: 吓僵，因恐惧而一动不动
collocations.example: She stood rigid with fear when the lights suddenly went out. 灯突然灭了，她吓得僵在原地。
The company's rigid regulations left no room for creativity, and its brightest employees soon drifted away. （议论文·管理·僵化）
A rigid education system that rewards only memorization can quietly stifle the very curiosity it should nurture. （议论文·教育批判）
Under his father's rigid discipline, the boy learned obedience but never once learned to laugh. （读后续写·成长·压抑）

collocations.translation: 因恐惧 / 寒冷而僵住
collocations.example: Rigid with cold, the stranded hikers huddled together and prayed for the first light of morning. （读后续写·求生·恶劣天气）

collocations.phrase: be rigid in one's thinking / views
collocations.example: Too rigid in his thinking to consider any new idea, the manager watched rival firms race ahead of his own. （议论文·守旧）
The soldier stood rigid at his post, refusing to flinch even as the storm howled around him. （读后续写·坚毅·人物）

collocations.translation: 严格死板的日程 / 时间表
collocations.example: Bound to a rigid schedule from dawn till dusk, the exchange students longed for one free afternoon to simply wander the old town. （读后续写·留学生活）

synonyms.example: Their coach was strict about punctuality, yet warm-hearted the moment training ended. （读后续写·人物·外严内暖）
synonyms.usage: strict 中性，可含关爱、合理的严格；rigid 贬义更重，强调'死板、不知变通'，批评意味明显。位置：strict/rigid 皆可作定语或表语。

synonyms.translation: 灵活的，可变通的（rigid 的反义）
synonyms.example: A good leader keeps rules flexible rather than rigid, bending them when kindness demands it. 好的领导让规则灵活而非死板，在需要善意时懂得变通。
synonyms.usage: 记忆点：rigid ↔ flexible 是一对反义词。写议论文批评'死板'用 rigid，主张'变通'用 flexible；短语 make the rules more flexible（让规则更灵活）委婉建议常用。

synonyms.example: His inflexible attitude meant that even the wisest suggestions fell on deaf ears. （议论文·固执）
synonyms.usage: inflexible 与 rigid 意思最接近，都指'不肯改变'；inflexible 略偏抽象（态度、规则），rigid 兼可形容具体物体的'坚硬'及身体的'僵直'。

synonyms.example: After the long flight her neck felt stiff, and she rolled her shoulders to shake off the ache. （读后续写·身体感受）
synonyms.usage: stiff 侧重物理上的'硬、不易弯曲'或身体酸僵，也可指举止拘谨；rigid 除物理僵硬外，更常引申为'制度/思想的死板'。

advancedExpressions.expression: sb. stood rigid, ... , unable to ...
advancedExpressions.example: She stood rigid at the doorway, her breath caught in her throat, unable to move, unable even to scream. （静态僵直+呼吸细节+双重unable并列，渲染极致恐惧）

advancedExpressions.expression: perhaps the rigid ... could be made more flexible
advancedExpressions.example: Perhaps the rigid rule that forbids all mobile phones could be made more flexible, allowing their use for study during breaks. （建议信·委婉口吻·make more flexible）

advancedExpressions.expression: rules that are too rigid ... rather than ...
advancedExpressions.example: Rules that are too rigid tend to crush initiative rather than guide it, for a mind hemmed in on every side can hardly learn to think for itself.

sentenceUpgrade.original: He was very strict and would not change the rules.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: So rigid was he in enforcing every rule that not even a tearful apology could soften his verdict, and the corridor fell silent as the boy trudged away. （读后续写·严苛·倒装）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: So + adj. 倒装(So rigid was he) + not even强调让步 + 细节动作(trudged away)收尾定格画面

sentenceUpgrade.original: The old system did not allow any change, so it failed.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Because the old system was so rigid that it slammed the door on every fresh idea, it gradually withered, overtaken by rivals bold enough to embrace change. （议论文·僵化之弊）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 原因状语从句(so...that) + 拟人隐喻(slammed the door on ideas) + 生动动词(withered) + 对比(overtaken by rivals)

classPractice.question: When the alarm suddenly went off, the boy stood ____ (rigid) with fear, unable to move a muscle.
classPractice.note: 考熟词僻义 rigid with fear（吓僵）；stand rigid 作系表结构，此处填形容词原形。

classPractice.question: 选 rigid / flexible：A wise teacher keeps the rules ____ enough to allow for special cases, rather than blindly strict.
classPractice.note: 反义辨析：主张变通用 flexible（灵活的），与 rigid（死板的）相对。

classPractice.question: 浪漫主义者拒绝遵循死板的规则。The Romantics refused to follow ____ ____.
classPractice.note: 呼应课文原句 rigid rules（死板的规则）；rigid 作定语修饰复数名词 rules。

translation: (underwent, undergone) 经历，经受
original_sentence: During that time, England was undergoing a process called industrialization.
readingExamples: During that time, England was undergoing a process called industrialization.
definitionEn:
(1) v. to experience or be subjected to something, especially a change, a difficult or unpleasant process
(2) v. to have a medical treatment, test, or operation done to one's body
(3) v. to pass through a period of development, transformation, or trial

posExamples.sentence: In the space of a single summer, the timid boy who had once flinched at every shadow underwent a remarkable change, returning to school with a steadiness in his eyes that no one could quite explain. （读后续写·人物蜕变）
I am writing to inform members that the sports hall will undergo major repairs next month, so all training sessions will be moved to the outdoor courts. （应用文·通知）

Any nation that hopes to thrive must be willing to undergo painful reforms, for progress rarely arrives without first demanding that we let go of comfortable old ways. （议论文·改革·呼应课文"industrialization"语境）
After undergoing months of gruelling rehabilitation, the young dancer finally rose onto her toes again — and the whole studio erupted in tears and applause. （读后续写·康复·坚持）

wordForms.other: 特殊变化(不规则)·undergo - underwent - undergone，读音 /ˌʌndəˈɡəʊ/。构词法：under-(在…之下/经受) + go(走→经历)。同族 under- 词：undertake(承担) / undergo(经历) / understand(理解)。注意：undergo 后接名词（undergo changes），不接不定式；being 结构用 undergo doing 少见，通常 undergo + 名词。

collocations.example: The town has undergone great changes. 这座城镇经历了巨大变化。
He had to undergo surgery on his knee. 他不得不接受膝盖手术。

collocations.translation: 经历一场变化 / 蜕变
collocations.example: Under his patient guidance, the rebellious teenager slowly underwent a transformation that astonished even his own parents. （读后续写·师恩·蜕变）
Just hours before she was due to undergo surgery, the girl scribbled a note thanking every nurse on the ward. （读后续写·感恩·医院）
During that era, England was undergoing a process of rapid industrialization that reshaped its cities forever. （议论文·历史·课文原句化用）
Having undergone years of hardship, the old fisherman spoke of the sea with a tenderness the young could not yet understand. （读后续写·沧桑·人物）
Every new bridge must undergo rigorous tests before a single car is allowed to cross. （议论文·安全·论证）
Before setting off, the volunteers underwent a week of intensive training in first aid and rescue. （应用文·活动准备）
In recent decades traditional handicrafts have undergone a remarkable revival, championed by a new generation proud of their heritage. （议论文·文化复兴）

synonyms.example: Studying abroad, she experienced both the sting of loneliness and the joy of unexpected friendship. （读后续写·留学·情感）
synonyms.usage: experience 最通用，好坏皆可，搭配范围极广；undergo 更正式，专指'经受'变化/治疗/苦难等（多为被动承受、常带艰难色彩）。句法：二者均及物，直接接名词。

synonyms.example: For three long months the miners endured darkness and hunger, yet their spirit never broke. （读后续写·苦难·坚韧）
synonyms.usage: endure 强调'忍耐痛苦并坚持下来'，带主观意志；undergo 中性，只表'经历/经受'这一事实，不强调忍耐。

synonyms.example: After all they had gone through together, the two friends knew nothing could ever pull them apart. （读后续写·友情）
synonyms.usage: go through 口语化，日常常用，搭配困难/阶段；undergo 书面正式，尤宜用于议论文、应用文及医疗/改革语境。

advancedExpressions.expression: having undergone ... , sb. emerged ...
advancedExpressions.example: Having undergone a trial that would have broken many, she emerged not bitter but wiser, her gentle strength shining brighter than ever before. （现在分词完成式+emerged对比升华人物成长）

advancedExpressions.expression: please be informed that ... will undergo ...
advancedExpressions.example: Please be informed that the library will undergo renovation from July 1st, and readers are kindly advised to return all borrowed books beforehand. （通知·正式被告知句式）

advancedExpressions.expression: only by undergoing ... can ... truly ...
advancedExpressions.example: Only by undergoing constant self-examination can a person truly grow, for it is in confronting our flaws that we discover the room to improve. （倒装+哲理收尾，强调变革的必要）

sentenceUpgrade.original: The boy changed a lot after that experience.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: After that unforgettable summer, the boy underwent a quiet but profound change: the fear that had once shadowed his every step gave way to a calm, unshakable confidence. （读后续写·蜕变）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: undergo升级change的搭配 + 对比结构(fear gave way to confidence) + 冒号引出具体转变 + 形容词递进(quiet but profound)

sentenceUpgrade.original: The country changed a lot during that time.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: During those turbulent decades, the country underwent a sweeping transformation, as smoking factories rose where quiet fields had once lain, and an old way of life was swept aside forever. （议论文·历史变革·呼应课文）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: undergo a sweeping transformation正式搭配 + as引导伴随变化 + 意象对比(factories vs fields) + 被动收尾(was swept aside)强化不可逆

classPractice.question: During that time, England was ____ (undergo) a process called industrialization.
classPractice.note: 呼应课文原句；过去进行时 was undergoing，undergo 的现在分词直接加 -ing。

classPractice.question: Over the past decade, the small fishing village has ____ (undergo) dramatic changes.
classPractice.note: 考不规则变化 undergo-underwent-undergone；现在完成时 has undergone。

classPractice.question: 选 undergo / experience：The patient will have to ____ major surgery next week.
classPractice.note: 接受手术等正式、被动承受的过程用 undergo（undergo surgery）更贴切、更正式。

translation: 工业化
original_sentence: During that time, England was undergoing a process called industrialization.
readingExamples: During that time, England was undergoing a process called industrialization.
definitionEn:
(1) n. the process by which an economy or country changes from one based mainly on agriculture to one based on manufacturing goods and industry
(2) n. the development of industries in a country or region on a wide scale, often accompanied by the growth of cities and factories
(3) n. the act of setting up mechanized industry as a dominant force in social and economic life

posExamples.sentence: As industrialization crept into the once-peaceful valley, the boy watched with a heavy heart while the meadow where he had chased butterflies gave way to a forest of smoking chimneys. （读后续写·环境变迁·失落）

I am writing to propose that our history club organize an exhibition on industrialization, so that fellow students may grasp how it reshaped not only the landscape but also the daily lives of ordinary people. （应用文·倡议信）
While industrialization undeniably lifted millions out of poverty, we must not turn a blind eye to the price it exacted from the environment and the working poor. （议论文·辩证分析）
The rapid industrialization of the nineteenth century, which transformed Britain into the workshop of the world, remains one of the most far-reaching turning points in human history. （议论文·历史评价）

wordForms.noun: industrialization (工业化); industry (工业,行业); industrialist (n. 实业家); industrialism (工业主义)
wordForms.adjective: industrial (工业的) / industrialized (已工业化的) / industrious (勤勉的——易混词!)
wordForms.adverb: industrially (在工业上); industriously (勤勉地——易混!)
wordForms.other: 构词链条(重点)·industry(工业) → industrial(工业的) → industrialize(使工业化) → industrialize + -ation → industrialization(工业化)。逐层加后缀：-al 构形容词、-ize 构动词、-ation 构名词。易混辨析：industrial(工业的) vs industrious(勤勉的、勤劳的)——形近义异，industrious 与 industry 的'勤奋'古义相关，考试高频陷阱。

collocations.example: England was undergoing a process of industrialization. 英国正经历工业化进程。
Rapid industrialization changed the country greatly. 快速的工业化极大地改变了这个国家。
The process of industrialization, once set in motion, swept through the countryside with unstoppable momentum. （议论文·历史进程）

collocations.translation: 快速的/大规模的工业化
collocations.example: Rapid industrialization brought unprecedented prosperity, yet it also crowded families into cramped, smoke-filled slums. （议论文·利弊）
During that time, the region was undergoing industrialization at a pace no one could have foreseen. （读后续写·时代背景）
The breakneck pace of industrialization left little room for the natural world to recover. （议论文·环境）
The invention of the steam engine did more than any single factor to accelerate industrialization across Europe. （议论文·科技影响）
Few writers captured the impact of industrialization on rural life more vividly than the Romantic poets. （议论文·文学）
Industrialization and urbanization advanced hand in hand, drawing waves of villagers into the ever-expanding cities. （议论文·社会变迁）
In the age of industrialization, the rhythm of human life was suddenly dictated by the factory clock. （读后续写·时代氛围）

synonyms.example: The mechanization of farming meant that a single machine could now do the work of a dozen labourers. （议论文·农业变革）
synonyms.usage: 侧重用机器取代人工的具体过程,范围窄于 industrialization,后者指整个经济社会向工业转型的宏观进程

synonyms.example: Industrialization was but one chapter in the sweeping story of the nation's modernization. （议论文·社会发展）
synonyms.usage: modernization 涵盖政治、科技、观念等全方位现代转型,industrialization 特指经济结构工业化,是现代化的一部分

advancedExpressions.expression: where once ... , now ... — such was the price of industrialization
advancedExpressions.example: Where once the river had run clear and songbirds had filled the dawn, now factory waste blackened the water and machines droned without pause — such was the price of industrialization. （今昔对比+破折号收束,续写渲染时代代价）

advancedExpressions.expression: learning from the lessons of industrialization, we ought to ...
advancedExpressions.example: Learning from the hard lessons of early industrialization, we ought to pursue development that never comes at the expense of our rivers and skies. （倡议信借古论今）

advancedExpressions.expression: for all the benefits industrialization has brought, it is a double-edged sword that ...
advancedExpressions.example: For all the prosperity industrialization has brought, it is a double-edged sword that has enriched nations while impoverishing the very environment on which they depend.

sentenceUpgrade.original: The town changed because of industrialization.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Almost overnight, it seemed, industrialization descended upon the sleepy town like an unstoppable tide — sweeping away the old cottages, the winding lanes and the unhurried mornings, and leaving in their place a restless world of steam, soot and ceaseless toil. （读后续写·环境变迁+比喻）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 比喻(like an unstoppable tide) + 三项并列意象(cottages, lanes, mornings) + 头韵与节奏(steam, soot)营造压迫感

sentenceUpgrade.original: Industrialization has both good and bad sides.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It would be short-sighted to condemn industrialization outright, for while it unquestionably scarred the natural landscape, it simultaneously unlocked levels of prosperity and opportunity that earlier generations could scarcely have imagined. （议论文·辩证）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: It would be short-sighted to...让步开篇 + for引导原因 + while让步状语 + simultaneously对比推进论证层次

classPractice.question: During the 19th century, Britain went through a rapid process of ____ (industry).
classPractice.note: 考构词链 industry→industrial→industrialize→industrialization；此处需名词'工业化'。

classPractice.question: 选 industrial / industrious：Bees are famous for being ____, working from dawn to dusk without rest.
classPractice.note: 形近易混：industrious=勤勉的（形容人/蜜蜂勤劳）；industrial=工业的。此处形容'勤劳'。

classPractice.question: 那时，英国正经历一个叫工业化的进程。At that time, England was undergoing a process called ____.
classPractice.note: 呼应课文原句 a process called industrialization；填名词工业化。

translation: vt. 拥护，支持，提倡 | n. 拥护者，支持者；律师
original_sentence: Instead, they advocated going back to nature.
readingExamples: Instead, they advocated going back to nature.
definitionEn:
(1) v. to publicly support or recommend a particular course of action, idea, or way of doing something
(2) n. a person who publicly supports or speaks in favour of a cause, policy, or group
(3) n. (chiefly Scottish & legal) a lawyer who pleads a case on someone's behalf in a court of law
(4) v. to argue in favour of something, especially by making a strong public case for it

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (苏格兰、南非等地的)出庭律师，辩护律师
uncommonMeanings.example: The young advocate rose in the hushed courtroom, straightened her gown, and began to plead her client's case with a quiet fire that silenced every whisper. （读后续写·法庭·人物出场）

posExamples.sentence: Standing on the windswept hilltop, the old poet advocated a return to the simple joys of nature, his voice trembling with a passion that the years had never dimmed. （读后续写·人物·信念）
In this letter I would like to advocate setting aside one afternoon each week for outdoor reading, an activity that I believe would nourish both our minds and our spirits. （应用文·建议信）
Those who advocate abolishing homework altogether overlook a crucial truth: without regular practice, even the brightest minds soon grow rusty. （议论文·观点反驳）
Throughout his life he remained a tireless advocate of the poor, championing their cause long after fashionable society had turned its back on them. （读后续写·人物评价）

wordForms.noun: advocate (拥护者,倡导者;出庭律师); advocacy (n. 拥护,提倡)
wordForms.other: 一词两读(重点)·作动词 v. 读 /ˈædvəkeɪt/，作名词 n. 读 /ˈædvəkət/(词尾弱读)——'名动异读'典型词，同类还有 graduate、estimate。构词法·ad-(向) + voc(声音,call) + -ate → '为…发声/呼吁'；词根 voc/vok 表'声音': voice, vocal, vocabulary, provoke。句法提示：advocate 后接名词或动名词(advocate doing)，不接不定式(不说 advocate to do)；主张从句用虚拟 advocate that sb (should) do。

idioms.translation: 故意唱反调(为激发讨论而站在对立面提出论点)
idioms.example: Let me play devil's advocate for a moment: is it truly wise to trust machines with decisions that shape human lives? （议论文·引出反方观点）

collocations.translation: 【课件】提倡/拥护/主张（某人）做某事（advocate 后接动名词）
collocations.example: Many experts advocate rewarding your child for good behaviour. 很多专家主张对你小孩的良好表现加以奖励。

collocations.translation: 【课件】主张……应做某事（从句用虚拟语气，should 可省略）
collocations.example: The report advocated that all buildings (should) be fitted with smoke detectors. 报告主张所有的建筑物都应安装烟雾探测器。

collocations.phrase: an advocate for / of sb / sth (n.)
collocations.example: She has always been an advocate for/of hospital workers. 她一直是医院工作人员的支持者。

collocations.translation: 提倡做某事（advocate 后接动名词）
collocations.example: They advocated going back to nature. 他们提倡回归自然。
She advocates for children's rights. 她为儿童权益发声。
He is a strong advocate of free education. 他是免费教育的坚定拥护者。

collocations.phrase: a strong / passionate advocate of sth
collocations.example: As a passionate advocate of lifelong learning, our headmaster reads a new book every single week. （应用文·人物描写）
Wordsworth stands out as a leading advocate of the belief that poetry should speak the language of ordinary men. （议论文·文学史）

collocations.phrase: advocate a policy / an approach / a return to
collocations.example: A growing number of educators now advocate an approach that values curiosity over rote memorization. （议论文·教育）
The committee advocated that every classroom be equipped with a small library corner. （应用文·提案，注意虚拟语气省略should）
He was a vocal advocate of environmental protection long before it became a popular cause. （议论文·环保）
Her tireless advocacy for equal education eventually reached the ears of the nation's leaders. （应用文·事迹）

synonyms.example: For thirty years he championed the rights of the voiceless, never once seeking reward or recognition. （读后续写·人物精神）
synonyms.usage: champion 情感更强烈,含'不畏艰难地捍卫、为其而战'之意,常搭配 rights/cause;advocate 更中性,侧重'公开主张、提倡'

synonyms.example: The campaign was launched to promote healthier eating habits among teenagers. （应用文·活动）
synonyms.usage: promote 侧重通过宣传、推动使某事发展或被接受,对象常为产品、活动、观念;advocate 侧重公开表态支持某主张

synonyms.example: I fully support your decision to devote your summer to volunteer work. （应用文·回信）
synonyms.usage: support 语气最普通、最常用,可用于人或事;advocate 更正式,含'主动公开提倡'的积极姿态

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·advocate 的三种句型（课件·Grammar）
advancedExpressions.expression: advocate (sb) doing sth / advocate that sb (should) do sth / an advocate for/of sth
advancedExpressions.example: Experts advocate rewarding good behaviour, and advocate that every building (should) be fitted with detectors; each of them is a firm advocate of safety. 专家主张奖励良好行为，也主张每栋楼都应装探测器；他们都是安全的坚定拥护者。（动名词/虚拟从句/名词搭配一并记）

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·'提倡/主张'(功能:议论文表态)
advancedExpressions.expression: advocate (doing) sth / call for sth / speak in favour of sth / be a strong advocate of sth
advancedExpressions.example: Many educators advocate learning through play, calling for lessons that spark curiosity rather than fear. 许多教育者提倡在游戏中学习，呼吁能激发好奇而非恐惧的课堂。（同义表态短语群，可替换升级）

advancedExpressions.expression: advocate / vocal / voice / vocabulary / provoke
advancedExpressions.example: An advocate raises his voice for a cause; the word itself hides the root 'voc' meaning 'to call'. 倡导者为某事发声，advocate 一词里就藏着表'呼喊'的词根 voc。（借词根记忆一组词）

advancedExpressions.expression: with unwavering conviction, sb. advocated ... , even when ...
advancedExpressions.example: With unwavering conviction, she advocated the path of kindness, even when the whole world seemed to reward cruelty. （even when让步凸显人物气节,续写升华段）

advancedExpressions.expression: I would strongly advocate that we ... , for the benefits are too great to ignore
advancedExpressions.example: I would strongly advocate that we set aside a 'green corner' in every classroom, for the benefits to both our mood and our air are simply too great to ignore. （建议信主张句+for引原因）

advancedExpressions.expression: far from advocating ..., I firmly believe that ...
advancedExpressions.example: Far from advocating a blind rejection of technology, I firmly believe that we must learn to make it serve, rather than enslave, us.

sentenceUpgrade.original: He supported protecting nature all his life.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: All his life he remained a steadfast advocate of the natural world, pleading its cause in verse and in speech, and never once wavering in his conviction that in wild places lay the truest medicine for the human soul. （读后续写·人物精神）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: advocate of替换普通support提升正式度 + 并列状语(in verse and in speech) + never once wavering强调坚定 + 抽象哲思收尾

sentenceUpgrade.original: I think we should read more books outdoors.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It is for this reason that I wholeheartedly advocate setting aside one afternoon each week for outdoor reading — a small change that, I am convinced, would refresh our weary minds and rekindle our love of learning. （应用文·建议信）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: It is for this reason that...强调句 + wholeheartedly advocate正式表主张 + 破折号补充说明 + 双动词递进(refresh, rekindle)

classPractice.question: Many experts advocate ____ (reduce) the amount of children's homework and also advocate that children ____ (give) more free time.
classPractice.note: 【课件】advocate doing sth 用动名词 → reducing；advocate that sb (should) do 从句虚拟，children 被给予 → (should) be given。

classPractice.question: Some immigrant ____ (advocate) worry that as hard financial times make it more difficult for natives to keep jobs, such measures will become more a vehicle for intolerance than integration.
classPractice.note: 【课件】此处需名词复数作主语（谓语 worry），advocate 作名词'支持者'→ advocates。

classPractice.question: She has always been an advocate ____ changes to English spelling, to make it easier to learn.
classPractice.note: 【课件】an advocate for/of sth ……的支持者/拥护者，介词用 for 或 of。

classPractice.question: The Romantic poets advocated ____ (go) back to nature rather than living among machines.
classPractice.note: 考搭配 advocate doing sth；advocate 后接动名词，不接不定式，故用 going。

classPractice.question: She has spent decades ____ ____ children who have no voice of their own. （用 advocate 恰当形式填'为…争取权益'）
classPractice.note: 考搭配 advocate for sb（为某人发声/争取权益）；spend time doing，用 -ing 形式。

classPractice.question: 他一生都是穷人的坚定拥护者。All his life he remained a strong ____ ____ the poor.
classPractice.note: 考名词搭配 an advocate of sth（…的拥护者）；此处 advocate 作名词，读 /ˈædvəkət/。

translation: 看法，信念；信仰；相信，信心
original_sentence: The poets also wrote about individual feelings and beliefs.
readingExamples: The poets also wrote about individual feelings and beliefs.
definitionEn:
(1) n. an acceptance that something is true or that something exists, especially without proof
(2) n. a firmly held opinion, conviction, or principle that guides one's actions
(3) n. trust or confidence in someone or something; faith
(4) n. (often plural) the religious or moral principles held by a person or group

posExamples.sentence: Even as the storm tore at the sails and the crew lost all hope, the old captain clung to a stubborn belief that the harbour lights would appear before dawn. （读后续写·绝境·信念）
It is my firm belief that a single act of kindness, however small, can ripple outward and brighten a dozen lives — and that is why I urge you all to join this campaign. （应用文·倡议书）
Contrary to popular belief, success is seldom the child of talent alone; more often, it is the hard-won reward of persistence. （议论文·观点驳斥）
The poets also wrote about individual feelings and beliefs, insisting that the inner world of a single human heart was worthy of the grandest verse. （议论文·文学主张）

wordForms.other: disbelief (n. 不相信)

idioms.translation: 难以置信，令人无法相信
idioms.example: When she opened the envelope and saw the scholarship offer, her joy was beyond belief. （读后续写·惊喜时刻）

idioms.translation: 与人们普遍看法相反
idioms.example: Contrary to popular belief, the quietest students in the class often harbour the boldest dreams. （议论文·反常识论点）

idioms.translation: 怀着……的信念，相信……
idioms.example: He set out at first light, in the firm belief that his friend was still alive somewhere in the mountains. （读后续写·出发·希望）

collocations.translation: 对……的信念/信任【课堂高频·in 是固定介词】
collocations.example: 课文原句：The poets also wrote about individual feelings and beliefs. 诗人们也书写个人的情感与信念。｜Her belief in kindness never wavered. 她对善良的信念从未动摇。
Her firm belief in second chances led her to forgive the very man who had wronged her. （读后续写·宽恕）
The Romantic poets held the belief that nature could heal what civilization had wounded. （议论文·文学）
It is my belief that reading widens our world far more than any journey ever could. （应用文·演讲）
Nothing could shake his belief that honesty would triumph in the end. （读后续写·坚守）
We must learn to respect those whose religious beliefs differ from our own. （议论文·包容）
The widely held belief that machines will render human effort obsolete is, in my view, deeply mistaken. （议论文·反驳）

collocations.phrase: restore / lose one's belief in sth
collocations.example: A single stranger's kindness restored her belief in the goodness of the world. （读后续写·感动）

synonyms.example: Through every setback she kept her faith that brighter days lay ahead. （读后续写·坚持）
synonyms.usage: faith 情感更浓、更主观,强调不需证据的信任或宗教信仰;belief 更中性,可指理性认定的观点,也可指信仰

synonyms.example: She spoke with such conviction that even her fiercest critics fell silent. （议论文·演讲力量）
synonyms.usage: conviction 强调经过思考后毫不动摇的确信,语气比 belief 更强;belief 可强可弱,泛指所相信的内容

synonyms.example: In my opinion, kindness costs nothing yet is worth everything. （议论文·观点）
synonyms.usage: opinion 侧重个人主观、可争议的看法,较随意;belief 常指更深层、更稳定、指导行为的信念

advancedExpressions.expression: belief in sth / beyond belief / contrary to popular belief / hold the belief that ...
advancedExpressions.example: 老师板书：belief 后接内容用 belief that 从句，接对象用 belief in sth（介词是 in，不是 of/to）；beyond belief=难以置信；contrary to popular belief=与大众看法相反。（课堂词块梳理）

advancedExpressions.expression: believe (v.) → belief (n.) → believable / unbelievable (adj.) → disbelief (n. 不相信)
advancedExpressions.example: 记忆钩子：动词 believe 以 -ve 结尾，名词 belief 变成 -f（类比 relieve→relief, prove→proof）；前缀 dis-/un- 表否定。（课堂拼写辨析）

advancedExpressions.expression: against all odds, sb. held fast to the belief that ...
advancedExpressions.example: Against all odds, the boy held fast to the belief that his mother would keep her promise, and it was this quiet faith that carried him through the darkest of nights. （against all odds+held fast to强化坚韧,续写心理线）

advancedExpressions.expression: it is my sincere belief that ... , and I therefore call on you to ...
advancedExpressions.example: It is my sincere belief that every voice matters, and I therefore call on each of you to speak up for what you know to be right. （倡议信信念+号召二连击）

advancedExpressions.expression: contrary to the widely held belief that ..., I would argue that ...
advancedExpressions.example: Contrary to the widely held belief that failure is something to be feared, I would argue that it is, in truth, the surest teacher we shall ever have.

sentenceUpgrade.original: He believed his friend would come back, so he waited.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Anchored by the unshakeable belief that his friend would return, he waited at the crossroads day after day, his eyes fixed on the horizon where the two roads met, refusing to let doubt take root in his heart. （读后续写·坚守·心理）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 过去分词短语开头(Anchored by...) + unshakeable belief强化 + day after day时间叠加 + refusing to let...拟人化心理描写

sentenceUpgrade.original: I think everyone can make a difference.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It is my unwavering belief that no act of kindness is ever too small to matter, and that each of us, in our own quiet way, holds the power to make the world a little warmer. （应用文·演讲）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: It is my unwavering belief that...正式主句 + no...ever too small双重否定强调 + in our own quiet way谦逊语气 + 温暖意象收束

classPractice.question: Contrary to popular ____, eating late at night does not necessarily make you gain weight.
classPractice.note: contrary to popular belief 与大众看法相反，固定短语，belief 不可数

classPractice.question: Nothing could shake his belief ____ honesty would win out in the end.
classPractice.note: belief 后接同位语从句用 that；接对象才用 belief in sb/sth

classPractice.question: 她美得令人难以置信。She was beautiful ____ ____.
classPractice.note: beyond belief 难以置信，作状语/表语

translation: 时代，年代
original_sentence: It was published in 1798 and marked the start of the Romantic era in poetry.
readingExamples: It was published in 1798 and marked the start of the Romantic era in poetry.
definitionEn:
(1) n. a long and distinct period of history with a particular feature or characteristic
(2) n. a period marked by a notable event, development, or the influence of a particular person or thing
(3) n. (geology) a major division of geological time, larger than a period

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (地质学)代(比'纪'更大的地质年代单位)
uncommonMeanings.example: Long before the first flower bloomed, in an era when giant reptiles ruled the land, the earth wore a face no human eye would ever behold. （读后续写·科普想象·远古）

posExamples.sentence: As the final curtain fell and the applause thundered on, the ageing actress understood that an era was ending — not just her own, but that of an entire generation who had grown up in the glow of the stage. （读后续写·时代落幕·感慨）
I am writing to invite you to our school's 'Voices of an Era' exhibition, where photographs and letters will bring the stirring decades of the last century vividly back to life. （应用文·邀请信）
We are living in an era of unprecedented change, and only those who dare to learn ceaselessly will keep pace with the world it is remaking around us. （议论文·时代主题）
Published in 1798, the collection marked the start of the Romantic era, when poets turned away from cold reason and looked instead to the human heart. （议论文·文学史）

idioms.idiom: mark the end / dawn of an era
idioms.translation: 标志一个时代的结束/开端
idioms.example: The launch of the first satellite marked the dawn of an era in which humanity's gaze would forever be fixed upon the stars. （议论文·科技里程碑）

idioms.translation: 一个时代的终结
idioms.example: When the old bookshop finally closed its doors, the whole town felt it was truly the end of an era. （读后续写·怀旧）

collocations.translation: 一个新时代/新纪元【课堂高频】
collocations.example: The invention of the printing press ushered in a new era of learning. 印刷机的发明开启了一个学习的新时代。
In the digital era, knowledge travels faster than ever before. 在数字时代，知识的传播比以往任何时候都快。

collocations.phrase: mark the start / dawn of an era
collocations.example: 课文原句：It was published in 1798 and marked the start of the Romantic era in poetry. 它于1798年出版，标志着诗歌浪漫主义时代的开端。
The novel captures the restless spirit of the Victorian era, torn between faith and doubt. （议论文·文学）
We stand at the threshold of an era of artificial intelligence, its promise as dazzling as its perils are grave. （议论文·科技）

collocations.phrase: usher in / herald a new era
collocations.example: The signing of the treaty ushered in a new era of cooperation between the two nations. （议论文·历史）
Handwritten letters seem to belong to a bygone era, yet nothing digital can quite recapture their warmth. （议论文·怀旧）
Many regard the 1980s as a golden era for Chinese poetry, when verse spilled from every campus and café. （议论文·文化）
Few writers have shaped an era as profoundly as Wordsworth shaped the Romantic age. （议论文·文学影响）

collocations.phrase: the start / dawn of an era
collocations.example: It was published in 1798 and marked the start of the Romantic era in poetry. （议论文·文学史）

synonyms.example: We live in the age of information, where knowledge travels faster than ever before. （议论文·时代）
synonyms.usage: 【课堂三词辨析 era/age/period】age 最口语，多见于固定名称(the Stone Age, the Ice Age, the Golden Age)，且可与 era 互换；era 略正式，强调有鲜明印记、常以重大事件为界的时代(the Romantic era)

synonyms.example: The Tang period is often celebrated as the height of classical Chinese poetry. （议论文·历史）
synonyms.usage: period 最中性、范围最广、可长可短，只是一段时间；era 特指较长且有独特特征、情感分量更重的时代——考试中'新时代/数字时代'首选 era/age，不用 period

synonyms.translation: (尤指开创新局面的)时期，纪元
synonyms.example: The moon landing opened a new epoch in the story of human exploration. （议论文·里程碑）
synonyms.usage: epoch 最书面庄重，尤指以重大转折事件为起点的纪元，语气比 era 更强；日常写作用 era 更稳妥

advancedExpressions.expression: a new era / the digital era / an era of + n. / usher in a new era / mark the dawn of an era
advancedExpressions.example: 老师板书：'开启新时代'高级说法 usher in / herald a new era；'在……时代'用 in the ... era 或 in an era of ...。（课堂词块梳理）

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·时代/时期辨析
advancedExpressions.expression: era ≈ age ≈ period ≈ epoch（分量：epoch > era ≈ age > period）
advancedExpressions.example: 写'数字时代'the digital era/age；写'一段短暂时期'the transition period；写'开天辟地的新纪元'a new epoch。（课堂选词升级）

advancedExpressions.expression: little did sb. know that this moment would mark the end of an era
advancedExpressions.example: Little did she know, as she waved from the platform, that this ordinary farewell would mark the end of an era she could never reclaim. （倒装+ mark the end of an era,续写埋下时代变迁的伏笔）
